_note: C1's work-type archetype per corporate function, keyed to the same seven function-group buckets config/function-groups.json already rolls departments into — reusing that rollup rather than inventing a second taxonomy for one skill. The assignment is per function-group, not per instance: a real Technology function might run a transactional service desk at one site and an advisory architecture team at another, and this config cannot see that split. Where it matters, read the trade-off case per instance rather than trusting the group-level archetype alone — that per-instance read is a later-phase gap, not something this file can fix.
_archetypes: transactional (payroll, accounts payable, recruitment administration, case processing — standardised, high-volume, centralizes well), advisory (business partnering — hybridizes between the centre and the business), site-operational (stays local; the frontline/clinical bulk of Operations is excluded from footprint work entirely by the clinical-presence rule before this ever applies).

Operations.rationale: Frontline delivery, logistics and clinical rosters — distributed by design. Clinical positions are excluded from footprint work outright; the non-clinical remainder (warehouse, fleet, maintenance) still runs local to where the work is.

Finance.rationale: Payroll, accounts payable/receivable and transaction processing dominate this bucket by headcount — the archetype the skill spec names first as centralizing well. FP&A and business-partnering roles inside Finance are the exception, not accounted for at the function-group level.

People.rationale: Recruitment administration and case processing dominate by headcount, per the skill spec's own example. Learning & development and organisational-design roles inside People read more as advisory and are not split out at this level.

Technology.rationale: Architecture, product and platform roles set standards the business executes against — the hybrid pattern. A pure transactional service desk inside Technology reads the same as the rest of the function here.

Commercial.rationale: Sales, marketing and customer-experience roles typically business-partner into local markets rather than run a standardised back-office process.

Corporate & Governance.rationale: Legal, risk, compliance and strategy are the textbook business-partnering functions — centre sets the framework, local leadership applies it.

Support Services.rationale: Facilities, procurement and records management are repetitive, standardised processes that centralize well.

default.rationale: No archetype is configured for this function group — advisory is the least presumptive default, since it recommends hybridizing rather than forcing a centralize-or-stay-local call Atlas has no basis for.
